defects.source_says: EO 12553 is headed 'Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986', signed 'THE WHITE HOUSE, February 25, 1986', FR Doc. 86-4455 filed 2-26-86, printed 51 FR 7237 on March 3, 1986 (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt). The claim's own source.signing_date (1986-02-25), mechanism text ('February 25, 1986'), judgment_reason ('1986-02-25') and research_rationale ('signed 1986-02-25') all give 1986. The recorded end date is three years before the revoking order existed and contradicts the claim's own mechanism and reasons.

defects.claim_says: the waiver is called 'the exhausted waiver' / 'the exhausted waiver command', while the end adopted is the 1986 revocation and exhaustion on 1966-09-12 is expressly not adopted
defects.source_says: Internal inconsistency: the claim cannot both describe the command as exhausted and date its end at a revocation twenty years later. Either the deeming is a continuing modification of EO 9721 (as saved by EO 10804 sec. 2) ended by EO 12553, or it was exhausted on taking effect; the claim must state one position consistently.

reasoning: Identity, text hashes, quoted spans, the clause inventory and the search record check out, and EO 12553 does revoke EO 11303 by number with no savings or effective-date wording, so a 1986-02-25 end by express revocation would be supportable (subject to consistent treatment of the exhaustion question). But the claim records the first end and whole-order end as 1983-02-25, a date that contradicts the cited source and the claim's own mechanism, signing_date and reasons, which all say February 25, 1986. A claim whose end date is wrong is rejected even though the actor and mechanism are right. The claim also calls the waiver 'exhausted' while adopting the 1986 revocation as the end of the command, an inconsistency to fix in any corrected version.
